pvp.smogon.title: Competitive pick
pvp.smogon.body: Smogon ranks Pokémon into usage-based tiers, and this one (or its evolution) shows up in the Gen 5 lists. This is based on Smogon Gen 5, and PokeMMO's own tiers may differ, so treat it as a strong hint rather than a rule.
pvp.smogon.more: Smogon's tiers go OU, UU, RU, then NU: OU holds the Pokémon people use most, and each step down is a lower usage bracket where those Pokémon don't have to compete with the best. A lower-tier Pokémon can still be great in PvP, because a good matchup matters more than a big name. This is Smogon Gen 5 data and PokeMMO's own tiers may differ, so check the current PokeMMO meta before you commit time to training one.

ev.title: EV yield
ev.body: Every Pokémon you defeat adds EVs to the Pokémon that fought it, and this is the stat it gives. Training EVs is how you push a stat above what its level alone gives you.
ev.more: A Pokémon can hold 252 EVs in one stat and 510 in total, and every 4 EVs in a stat adds 1 point at level 100. Most competitive teams put 252 into two stats and the leftover into a third. To train a stat, battle Pokémon that yield it until you hit the cap.

utility.pickup.title: Pickup
utility.pickup.body: A Pokémon with Pickup can find an item after a battle. Players keep one in their party while they grind or hunt, so items come in on the side.
utility.pickup.more: Pickup works from your party, so it costs a team slot but no extra time. It rewards the grinding you were going to do anyway.

utility.synchronize.title: Synchronize
utility.synchronize.body: Put a Synchronize Pokémon first in your party and wild Pokémon have a 50% chance to share its nature. Players keep one of each useful nature to hunt and breed with.
utility.synchronize.more: Nature matters because it raises one stat by 10% and lowers another, so the right nature is the difference between a good Pokémon and a perfect one. Bring a Synchronize lead of the nature you want, and you will meet that nature half the time instead of rarely.

utility.compoundeyes.title: Compound Eyes
utility.compoundeyes.body: A Pokémon with Compound Eyes in the lead slot makes wild Pokémon more likely to be holding their items. It also raises the accuracy of its own moves.
utility.compoundeyes.more: Use it when you are farming a wild Pokémon for the item it holds. Pair it with Thief or Covet to steal an item without fighting for it.

utility.frisk.title: Frisk
utility.frisk.body: When a Frisk Pokémon enters battle it shows the held item of the opposing Pokémon. Lead with it when you are hunting for a specific item, so you know whether a wild Pokémon is worth the fight.
utility.frisk.more: In PvP the same effect tells you what your opponent's Pokémon is holding on the turn it comes out, such as a Choice item or a berry, which changes how you play the rest of the match.

utility.payday.title: Pay Day
utility.payday.body: Pay Day scatters coins when it hits, and you collect them as money once the battle ends. How much you get scales with the level of the Pokémon using it, so it is a steady way to earn money while you grind.
utility.payday.more: Money from Pay Day adds up when you are already fighting. Use it as your attack against wild Pokémon you are going to defeat anyway.

utility.thief.title: Thief
utility.thief.body: Thief takes the held item from the target if your Pokémon is not holding one. That lets you collect items from wild Pokémon without defeating them.
utility.thief.more: Make sure the Pokémon using Thief holds nothing first. Once it has stolen an item, it stops stealing until you take that item off it.

utility.covet.title: Covet
utility.covet.body: Covet hits and then takes the target's held item, as long as your Pokémon is not holding one. It works like Thief, so use it to collect items from wild Pokémon.
utility.covet.more: Covet and Thief do the same job, so whichever one your Pokémon learns by level-up is the one to use. You pick it for the item, not the damage.

utility.falseswipe.title: False Swipe
utility.falseswipe.body: False Swipe can never knock a Pokémon out, it always leaves the target with at least 1 HP. It is a catching tool: weaken the wild Pokémon without defeating it, then throw a ball.
utility.falseswipe.more: A Pokémon at low HP is much easier to catch. Pair False Swipe with a status move like Spore to make a catch very safe.

utility.sweetscent.title: Sweet Scent
utility.sweetscent.body: Sweet Scent lowers the evasion of the target in battle. That helps moves that can miss, like sleep moves, land more often.
utility.sweetscent.more: Evasion boosts make your moves miss more, and Sweet Scent pushes the target the other way. It is a support move, so you only run it when accuracy is the problem.

utility.spore.title: Spore
utility.spore.body: Spore puts the target to sleep and hits reliably. A sleeping wild Pokémon is easier to catch, so Spore pairs well with False Swipe.
utility.spore.more: Sleep also stops the target from attacking for a few turns. That gives you time to weaken it with False Swipe and throw balls.

story.title: Story
story.body: A Story pick is a Pokémon that makes the main storyline easier: it is strong against the gym leaders and Elite Four, or it is easy to get early. If you want to breeze through the campaign, this one is worth catching and training.
story.more: Story picks are our own suggestions for a first playthrough, not a competitive ranking. A Pokémon can be great in the story and weak in PvP, so treat this as advice for getting through the game, then decide what is worth keeping for the long run.

tips.63: Abra uses Teleport on its first turn, so put it to sleep with a faster Pokémon or throw a ball right away.
tips.64: Wild Kadabra can still flee with Teleport, so open with a sleep move or a ball rather than an attack.
tips.74: Geodude learns Selfdestruct at level 19, so higher-level ones can blow themselves up; catch them quickly or put them to sleep.
tips.75: Graveler can use Selfdestruct or Explosion and end the encounter, so put it to sleep or catch it quickly.
tips.100: Voltorb learns Selfdestruct at level 19 and can faint itself to end the encounter, so catch it quickly or put it to sleep.
tips.101: Electrode is very fast and can use Selfdestruct or Explosion before you act, so open with a ball or a faster sleep move.
tips.109: Koffing learns Selfdestruct at level 24, so higher-level ones can end the fight themselves; put them to sleep or catch them quickly.
tips.110: Weezing can use Selfdestruct or Explosion and end the encounter, so put it to sleep before you start throwing balls.
tips.113: Chansey is a very rare spawn in Kanto's Safari Zone, so bring plenty of Safari Balls and expect it to take a while.
tips.132: Ditto transforms into a copy of your lead Pokémon, so lead with something weak or harmless to keep the fight easy.
tips.133: Eevee is a rare spawn on Kanto's Route 17, so expect to search for a while before one appears.
tips.147: Dratini is caught by fishing, for example in Johto's Dragon's Den, Kanto's Safari Zone and Sinnoh's Mt. Coronet.
tips.177: Natu learns Teleport at level 10, so higher-level Natu can flee; put it to sleep before you start throwing balls.
tips.202: Wobbuffet only fights back with Counter, Mirror Coat and Destiny Bond, so lower its HP with status damage or weak hits instead of big attacks.
tips.204: Pineco learns Selfdestruct at level 6, so even low-level ones can faint themselves; lead with a sleep move.
tips.246: In Unova, Larvitar comes from dust clouds in Twist Mountain, so step into any dust cloud you see there.
tips.280: Ralts is a rare spawn and can know Teleport from level 15, so open with a sleep move if you find a higher-level one.
tips.281: Wild Kirlia can know Teleport and flee, so put it to sleep before you start throwing balls.
tips.349: Feebas is a special Super Rod catch on Route 119 and in Mt. Coronet, so expect to fish for a while.
tips.371: Bagon is a rare spawn in Meteor Falls and Altering Cave, so expect to search for a while.
tips.374: Beldum only knows Tackle and Take Down, and Take Down's recoil can make it faint itself, so don't leave it at low HP.
tips.425: Higher-level Drifloon can use Selfdestruct, so put it to sleep or catch it quickly.
tips.443: Gible lives in Wayward Cave, whose hidden entrance is under the Cycling Road on Route 206.
tips.529: Drilbur only comes from dust clouds in Unova caves like Wellspring Cave and Chargestone Cave, so step into any dust cloud you see.
tips.570: Zorua only appears in hordes in Lostlorn Forest, and Illusion can make it look like a different Pokémon until it takes a hit.
